readerAnswers.scope: Cursor launched Projects in beta on September 10 for longer software jobs, from adding a feature to building a whole app.
readerAnswers.mechanism: A Project runs on a computer in the cloud—online rather than on your laptop—so closing your laptop does not stop that part of the job. If testing is needed on your own computer, Cursor says the coordinator starts a local agent there.
readerAnswers.boundary: If testing is needed on your own computer, Cursor says the coordinator starts a local agent there.
readerAnswers.relevance: It can be relevant to a personal website/app or a larger work project when the job is bounded and inspectable.

terms.coordinator: A coordinator is the agent that plans the job and sends pieces to other agents; Cursor says the other agents write the code.

explainBack: A Cursor Project keeps the context of one longer job. A coordinator sends pieces to agents, cloud work can keep going after the laptop closes, and testing on the reader’s machine uses a local agent; the reader still checks the result.
unseenTransfer: When another AI product says it can keep working, ask where it runs, what handoff occurs when local access is needed, and who checks the completed work.
